At 11a.m. October 21, Sung Wen Chong visited the
Commercial Press and was accordingly arrested by C.D.C.
344.

（批：S.L. 22.10.41）

Sung emphatically denied that he had intimidated Mr.
Wong over the telephone, or that he had visited the
Commercial Press with several undesirables during the
afternoon of October 7.

He further asserted that his visit to the Commercial
Press on October 21 was for the purpose of removing some
personal property.

Mr. Wong later attended the Station and after giving
due consideration to all points requested that no
criminal action be taken against Sung provided he signed
a statement promising not to molest him again. This Sung
did.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... 22 ... SPECIAL ...）

For obvious reasons Mr. Wong's request was complied
with there being a desire on his part not to antagonise
his loyal employees.

Sung was released on promising not to create further
trouble.

他进一步声称，其于10月21日造访商务印书馆的目的是为了取回一些个人财物。

黄先生随后前往警局，在充分考虑各项情况后要求，只要宋文冲签署一份承诺不再骚扰他的声明，便不对其采取刑事行动。宋文冲照办了。

page_data.en:
During the evening of October 8th,1941,
Mr.K.S.Wong ( 王 ),Manager of the Commercial
Press,211 Honan Road, telephoned D.I.Moir reporting
that he had reasons to believe that certain ex-
employees of the Commercial Press were intimidating
him and making his life miserable.

D.I.Moir later interviewed Mr.Wong and
elicited from him that the trouble is the out-come
of the strike which was recently settled. It will
be recalled that the strike at the Commercial
Press lasted several weeks.

This settlement resulted in the Company
dispensing with the services of several of their
employees.

The dismissed employees received adequate
reparation,i.e.~9 months pay,(approved by Social
Welfare Bureau) and signed a document relieving
the Commercial Press of further obligations so
far as they were concerned.

Amongst those whose services were dispensed
with were three agitators and trouble-makers,
namely (1) Tang Wen Cheong( 陳文昌 ),(2) Soeng Shing
Kang ( 宋鑫廣 ) and (3) Tsu Wei Sim ( 朱威荃 ).

These men have apparently self-appointed
themselves leaders of the dismissed workers and
to all intents and purposes are out to make as
much trouble as they can.

They are arrogant individuals and by their
tactics it is quiet obvious that they intend
to make Mr.Wong's life miserable.
page_data.zh:
1941年10月8日晚间，
商务印书馆经理、河南路211号的王康生先生（Mr. K.S. Wong）致电莫尔侦探督察（D.I. Moir），报告称他有理由相信某些商务印书馆的前雇员正在恐吓他，使他的生活变得痛苦不堪。

莫尔侦探督察随后会见了王先生，并从他那里了解到，这场麻烦是最近刚解决的罢工事件的后果。众所周知，商务印书馆的罢工持续了数周。

此次和解导致公司解雇了几名员工。

被解雇的员工获得了充分的赔偿，即约9个月的工资（经社会福利局批准），并签署了一份文件，免除商务印书馆对他们进一步的义务。

在被解雇的人员中，有三名煽动者和捣乱分子，即 (1) 唐文冲（Tang Wen Cheong，原文括号内注陳文昌），(2) 宋鑫广（Soeng Shing Kang）和 (3) 朱威荃（Tsu Wei Sim）。

这些人显然自封为被解雇工人的领袖，并且实际上正竭力制造尽可能多的麻烦。

他们是傲慢的人，从其策略来看，很明显他们意图让王先生的生活变得痛苦不堪。

page_data.en:

The Commercial Press are under no obligation
whatsoever to these men and Mr.Wong is not obliged
to see them.

As a result of their recent activities Mr.
Wong has been obliged to restrict his activities to
such an extent that it is now considered necessary
to afford him Police protection.

At 10.40 a.m. October 2,1941,Zung Wen Chong,
Soong Shing Kung, and Tsu Wei Shu forced their way
into Mr.Wong's office and demanded that he dispense
with the services of certain coolies employed by
the Hung Zung Cleaning Company and reinstate some of
dismissed workers.

Mr.Wong stated that his firm was not prepared
to entertain such a proposition and that they were
under no obligation to their former employees.

Police were called and the intruders were
requested to leave the building. They were also
warned to keep away.(See C.Misc.838/41).

During the afternoon of Friday,October 3,1941,
some-one telephoned Mr.Ting Yang Hwei(      ),who is
in charge of the General Affairs Department.

The anonymous caller who Mr.Ting Yang Hwei

商务印书馆对这些人不负有任何义务，王先生也没有义务会见他们。

由于他们最近的活动，王先生被迫大幅限制自己的活动范围，以至于现在认为有必要为他提供警察保护。

1941年10月2日上午10时40分，曾文冲（Zung Wen Chong）、宋新庚（Soong Shing Kung）和朱维书（Tsu Wei Shu）强行闯入王先生的办公室，要求他解雇宏钟清洁公司（Hung Zung Cleaning Company）雇佣的某些苦力，并重新雇用一些被解雇的工人。

王先生表示，他的公司不准备接受这样的提议，并且他们对前雇员不负有任何义务。

警方被叫来，入侵者被要求离开大楼。他们还受到警告，不得靠近。（参见 C.Misc.838/41）。

1941年10月3日（星期五）下午，有人给负责总务部的丁仰辉先生（Mr. Ting Yang Hwei，姓名空缺）打电话。

这位匿名来电者，丁仰辉先生

page_data.en:
-3-

recognised by his voice to be Zung Wen Chong spoke
as follows:
    "If anything happens to Mr.Wong, I cannot be
    responsible."
    As a result of this message Mr.Wong became very
alarmed and has been compelled to restrict his movements.
    Further developments occurred at about 5.30p.m.
October 7, when Zung Wen Chong entered the Commercial
Press and enquired of the firm's private detective one
named Sung Kwei Moh (沈桂木) if Mr.Wong was in the
office. The private detective saw that Zung Wen Chong
was accompanied by five male Chinese of the loafer
class, who were standing on the opposite side of the
road. Zung Wen Chong told the private detective that
he resented Mr.Wong's action in calling in the Police
on October 2.
    He later left the building and was seen to
converse with the loafers.
    Mr.Wong was not in at the time, but it is
his usual custom to leave the building at about 5.30p.m.
daily.
    It is not quite apparent that the purpose of
Zung's visit with the loafers was either to assault
Mr.Wong or create a public scene when he was leaving
page_data.zh:
-3-

通过声音认出是曾文冲（Zung Wen Chong），他说：
    “如果王先生发生任何意外，我不负责任。”
    由于这条消息，王先生变得非常惊恐，并被迫限制自己的行动。
    进一步的进展发生在10月7日下午5时30分左右，当时曾文冲进入商务印书馆，并向该公司的一名私家侦探沈桂木（Sung Kwei Moh）询问王先生是否在办公室。私家侦探看到曾文冲由五名中国男性游手好闲之徒陪同，他们站在马路对面。曾文冲告诉私家侦探，他对王先生在10月2日召警的行为感到不满。
    他随后离开大楼，并被看到与那些游手好闲之徒交谈。
    王先生当时不在，但他通常的习惯是每天下午5时30分左右离开大楼。
    曾文冲与游手好闲之徒来访的目的尚不完全清楚，是为了在王先生离开

the premises.

It is also known that Zung Wen Chong was
loitering in the vicinity of the Commercial Press
at about 9 a.m. October 8. Detectives failed to
locate him.

Necessary precautions have been taken,meanwhile
detectives are continuing enquiries in an endeavour
to locate Zung Wen Chong.

If these men are permitted to continue with such
tactics it will be impossible for Mr.Wong to attend
to his business, and further more if they get away
with it they will eventually exercise much control
over the loyal employees.

A determined effort will be made to locate
Zung Wen Chong.

Enquiries proceeding.

Ex-employees of the Commercial Press call upon Manager.

Sir,

At 10.40a.m. October 2nd, 1941, Mr. Y.S. Wang, Manager of the Commercial Press, 211 Honan Road, telephoned the Station reporting that three of the ex-employees, namely Sung Hsing Keng (宋新庚), Tsu Wei Hei (朱維黑) and Zung Vung Chong (曾文昌) had entered his office and were annoying him.

These men who claimed to represent dismissed employees had called upon Mr. Wang for the purpose of insisting that the company employ some of the dismissed employees as cleaning coolies and dispense with the services of the Hung Sang Cleaning Company who have done this work for several years.

Mr. Wang stated that his Company was not prepared to entertain such a proposition and that they were under no obligation to any of their former employees.

The three intruders left the building when advised to do so by detectives.

Detectives are keeping in touch with Mr. Wang.

In connection with the strike of 1,131 employees of

to nine months' wages (without rice allowance) to 544
employees whose services are to be dispensed with owing
to the unfavourable financial condition of the company.
The management also promised to reinstate the discharged
employees when the company needs hands in future.

It is to be reported that since the "Lock Out" declared by the Commercial Press on April 22, 1941, there have been no disturbances among the employees of the Printing Department located at No.694 Bubbling Well Road. Commercial Press Ltd. - Strike.

At 7.5p.m.22/4/41 a telephone message was received
from Mr. Lee,manager of the Commercial Press, reporting
that some of the senior employees of the firm were being
detained by strikers on the firm's premises at 211 Honan
Rd. C.D.S.337 and D.S.I.Mason attended and found all
the grilles locked. The strikers,under the leadership
of one Tsao Zee Liang(赵紫良)readily opened the
grille however,and admitted detectives. They then escort-
ed them to a 1st floor office where Mr.C.L.Bau(鲍学林)
Assistant manager, and Mr.K.S.Wong(王康生),secretary,
were privately interviewed.

Mr.Bau and Mr.Wong informed the undersigned that
at about 3p.m. 22/4/41,the staff had declared a "sit down"
strike and passed a resolution to remain on the premises
without food for 48 hours. When questioned as to whether
they were being detained against their will,both Mr.Bau
and Mr.Wong declared that they were staying on the
premises willingly,although the inference was that the
strikers expected them to remain. Mr. Bau and Mr.Wong
were then asked definitely if they desired to leave with
Police assistance. They were opposed to this and maintain-
ed that they would rather remain than aggravate the
strike situation by the use of Police assistance. The
undersigned accordingly left the premises,promising to

商务印书馆有限公司 - 罢工。

1941年4月22日晚上7时5分，接到商务印书馆经理李先生的电话留言，报告称该公司部分高级雇员正被罢工者扣留在河南路211号的公司场所内。中央侦探社第337号警员（C.D.S.337）及副督察梅森（Mason）到场，发现所有铁栅门均已上锁。然而，罢工者在一名叫赵紫良（Tsao Zee Liang）的人的带领下，轻易打开了铁栅门，并允许侦探进入。随后，他们护送侦探到一楼的一间办公室，在那里私下询问了副经理鲍学林（C.L. Bau）先生和秘书王康生（K.S. Wong）先生。

鲍先生和王先生告知本人，1941年4月22日下午3时许，员工宣布“静坐”罢工，并通过决议在场所内禁食48小时。当被问及是否被违背意愿扣留时，鲍先生和王先生均声明他们是自愿留在场所内的，尽管暗示罢工者期望他们留下。随后明确询问鲍先生和王先生是否希望在警方协助下离开。他们反对这样做，并坚持认为，与其通过警方介入加剧罢工局势，不如留下来。因此，本人离开场所，承诺

September 15, 1939. Afternoon Translation

THE AFFAIRS OF THE COMMERCIAL PRESS

The "Sin Wan Pao" publishes the following notice inserted by the Commercial Press:-
Yesterday a notice was published in the newspapers by a so-called "Entire body of employees of the Commercial Press" addressed to the company's partners and the public. As this notice affects the reputation of this firm, we hereby make the following statement in reply:-
The notice says that "the firm cares only about its own interests and is without sympathy", that "the firm has changed its attitude since the resumption of operations," and that "the measures for the purchase of rice by the company to be sold at a low price to the workers be opposed."
After the outbreak of hostilities, the business of the firm became much depressed. With a view to maintaining the livelihood of the employees, the entire body of workers was retained and not a single one was dismissed, only their pay was reduced. Subsequently the pay of the junior employees was gradually restored to the original rate. By the beginning of August this year, the pay of all the employees had been restored to their old scale while those whose pay is small have had their pay increased in view of the high cost of living.
Later, when the price of rice began to rise, the employees demanded allowances. General Manager Wang had to consider the situation for the company was already over-burdened by the recent salary increases.
Unexpectedly the employees organized an association and went on a go-slow strike on August 22 but resumed work on August 31 when it was promised that pay would be issued for the period of the strike. On September 1, they started a second go-slow strike and published a notice in the papers stating that the promises of the firm had not been kept. Just as the management of the Press was going to give a reply, the employees resumed operations on the advice of the senior staff. General Manager Wang had kept his promise not to deduct the wages of the workers for the period of the strike.
Meanwhile, General Manager Wang had devised certain measures for the purchase of rice. The management of the Press had agreed to advance a sum of $10,000 for the purchase of rice to be sold to the employees at $12 per picul when the market price of rice is quoted at $20 per picul. 400 piculs of rice would be supplied every month, which would have meant an expenditure of about $3,200 by the firm. 商务印书馆事件

《新闻报》刊登了商务印书馆插入的如下通告：-
昨日，一家所谓“商务印书馆全体职员”在报纸上发布了一则致公司合伙人和公众的通告。由于此通告影响本行声誉，特此发表声明答复如下：-
该通告称“本行只顾自身利益，缺乏同情心”，称“自恢复营业以来，本行改变了态度”，并称“反对公司为以低价向工人出售大米而采取的采购措施”。
战事爆发后，本行业务大幅萧条。为了维持员工生计，保留了全体员工，未解雇一人，仅降低了薪资。随后，初级员工的薪资逐渐恢复至原有水平。到今年8月初，所有员工的薪资已恢复至旧有标准，鉴于生活成本高企，低薪员工的薪资有所增加。
后来，当米价开始上涨时，员工要求发放津贴。王总经理不得不考虑这一情况，因为公司近期加薪已负担过重。
出乎意料的是，员工组织了一个协会，并于8月22日举行怠工罢工，但在承诺支付罢工期间工资后，于8月31日复工。9月1日，他们开始了第二次怠工罢工，并在报纸上发表通告，声称公司未履行承诺。正当印书馆管理层准备回复时，员工在高级职员的建议下恢复了运营。王总经理信守诺言，未扣除工人罢工期间的工资。
与此同时，王总经理制定了某些采购大米的措施。印书馆管理层同意预付10,000美元用于购买大米，当市场米价为每担20美元时，以每担12美元的价格出售给员工。每月供应400担大米，这意味着公司支出约3,200美元。员工的要求是因为高昂的

AUG 23 1939

Commercial Press Men
Go on Strike
Demand for “Allowances”
Rejected

Their demand for “allowances” by reason of the increased cost of living consequent upon the decrease in the value of the Chinese dollar having been turned down by their management, employees of the Shanghai office of the Commercial Press Ltd., the biggest Chinese publishing firm, in Foochow Road declared a sit-down strike commencing yesterday.

The striking employees sent printed pamphlets in both Chinese and English to various organizations appealing for the sympathy of the public in their present trouble. It was stated that negotiations for “allowances” to compensate the loss resulting from the drop of the Chinese dollar had been carried out with the head of the Personnel Department of the company, but the demand was turned down.

The responsible persons of the company who are in Hongkong, where the head office of the company has moved since the hostilities, were stated to be most firm in their stand against any increase of wages. Mr. Wang Yung-wu, manager of the firm, was criticized in a Chinese letter addressed to the public appealing for help.

商务印书馆员工
举行罢工
“津贴”要求
被拒

罢工员工向各组织发送了中英文印刷小册子，呼吁公众对其目前的困境表示同情。据称，就补偿因中国货币下跌造成损失的“津贴”问题与公司人事部主任进行了谈判，但该要求被驳回。

据悉，公司负责人在战事发生后总部迁往的香港立场坚定，反对任何加薪。在一封致公众求助的中文信中，公司经理王云五（Wang Yung-wu）先生受到批评。

AUG 23 1939
23964

'We Want Rice'
Demands Made
To Print Firm

Sit-Down Strike Staged
By Commercial Press
Employees Here

"Which, Mediation or . . .?" demanded Chinese employees of the Commercial Press yesterday when they instituted a "We Want Rice" sit-down-strike in the premises of the company on Honan Road near Foochow Road yesterday.

The question was put to the general public in the form of posters, written both in English and Chinese, asking for co-operation in pressing their demands for a wage increase to meet the situation which has arisen as the result of the fall in exchange and the current rice shortage in Shanghai.

Although a detail of police was ordered to the scene of the strike immediately after the notices had been displayed outside the company's premises, at the corner of Honan and Foochow Roads, just west of the Central Station, the services of the squad were not required up to a late hour last night.

Note To Customers

Because of the strike, declared yesterday morning, business on the premises of the Commercial Press store was at a standstill. As they entered the place, customers were handed a typewritten note, which stated:

"Dear customers: Under unbearable pressure of living standards here we are obliged to take a claim of sit-down strike as a protest against the company's unfair treatment and consequently we regret that we are not in a position to be of any service to you during this moment of our struggle. Unless the authorities of this company realize their misrule and find some means to save us from hunger, there will be no hope to keep us quietly at work. Should you sympathize with us, please send your help and support for the sake of Justice and Humanity."

In a letter to the English language press, the sit-down strikers declared:

"Being hard pressed by the unprecedented drop of the Chinese dollar recently the employees of the Commercial Press Ltd. here in Shanghai, demanded rightful allowances commensurate with the ever rising cost of living.

"After undertaking several negotiations between the representatives of the employees and the management, represented by the head of the personnel department, the result was nil.

"As it is beyond reason to keep our body and soul together, we have no other means but to take this drastic action, viz., sit-down strike.

“我们要米”
向印刷公司提出诉求

商务印书馆员工在此举行静坐罢工

昨日，商务印书馆的中国员工在位于河南路近福州路的公司 premises（办公处所）内发起了一场“我们要米”的静坐罢工，当时他们质问道：“是调解，还是……？”

这一问题以中英文书写的海报形式向公众提出，呼吁公众合作，向资方施压以满足其加薪要求，从而应对因汇率下跌及上海当前大米短缺所造成的局面。

尽管在张贴告示后，警方立即派遣分队前往位于中央车站以西、河南路与福州路转角处的公司门外罢工现场，但直至昨晚深夜，并未需要动用该警队。

致顾客须知

由于昨日上午宣布罢工，商务印书馆门市部的业务陷入停顿。顾客进入时，会收到一份打字的通知，内容如下：

“尊敬的顾客：鉴于此处生活水准的压力已令人难以忍受，我们被迫采取静坐罢工的诉求，以抗议公司的不公待遇，因此我们遗憾地表示，在我们斗争的此刻，无法为您提供任何服务。除非本公司当局认识到其管理不善，并找到使我们免于饥饿的办法，否则我们无法安心工作。若您同情我们，请为了正义与人道给予帮助和支持。”

在给英文报刊的一封信中，静坐罢工者声明：

“由于近期法币空前暴跌，商务印书馆有限公司驻上海的员工要求获得与生活成本不断上升相称的正当津贴。

“在员工代表与由人事部门负责人代表的管理层进行多次谈判后，结果一无所获。

“由于维持生计已不合常理，我们别无他法，只能采取这一激烈行动，即静坐罢工。

CHINA PRESS.
DEC 20 1938.
600 Workers
Of Publishing
House Strike

Commercial Press Plant
Remains Idle For
Two Hours

RESTORATION OF
OLD WAGES ASKED

Settlement Of Dispute
Believed To Be
Distant

（右上角印章内容：S. D. REGISTRY / No. S. B. D. - 06644 / Date ____）

Six hundred workers in the fac-
tories of the Commercial Press
went on a two-hour sit-down strike
early yesterday morning after fail-
ing to conduct negotiations with
the company for the re-instatement
of the workers' wage scale to its
pre-war level.

The dispute between the workers
and the company began a fortnight
ago, where representatives of the
workers presented the following de-
mands to the company:
1. Recognition of the "Com-
mercial Press Workers' Co-operative
Association," the workers' newly
organized union;
2. A subsidy to cover the expan-
ditures of the Association and
3. Restoration of the workers'
wages to their pre-war level.

Company Unyielding
On receipt of these three de-
mands, officials of the Company
communicated with Mr. Wang Yun-
wo, President of the Company, now
in Hongkong. Replying, Mr. Wang,
THE CHINA PRESS learned, instructed
the officials that "to accept the
workers' terms would be tantamount
to suicide in view of the difficulties
already confronting the Company."
In accordance with the Presi-
dent's instructions, and on the
ground that the union is not legally
existent, officials of the company
here refused to negotiate with re-
presentatives of the workers.

Statement Issued
In an official statement yesterday
evening, the company set forth its
position regarding the present dis-
pute with the workers.
Explaining why it would not re-
store the workers' wages to their
pre-war levels, the statement re-
viewed the amount of damages suf-
fered sustained by the company as
a result of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities.
Losses amounting to **〔此处转录不清〕**
are said to have been sustained by
the Company as a result of the
bombing of the company's plants in
Chapei and the destruction of
the branch in Wuchow.
Losses sustained by the Com-
pany, the statement continued,
were not real, but were paper
losses which fell, it was stated,
upon the shoulders of the stock-
holders.

Heavy Losses Sustained
Owing to the Company's heavy
losses, the statement added, the
company was compelled to reduce
its capital from $5,000,000 to
$2,500,000. The reduction was ef-
fected by writing off 50 per cent
of the climbing foreign exchange.
Altogether, the statement added,
less than ten of the Company's 30
branches in all parts of China are
still operating, and even their sales
receipts are much lower today than
they were before the war.

Workers Well Treated
Concerning the company's treat-
ment of its workers, the statement
revealed that despite mounting costs
of production and diminishing sales
returns, practically no employees
had been laid off by the company.
When hostilities broke out in
Shanghai, the statement said, the
company's factories were forced to
discontinue operations. The work-
ers, however, were not laid off com-
pletely but given a certain amount
of allowance to tide over the crisis.
All these workers have now been
re-hired, it was stated, either to
resume work in the local factories
or to be sent to other factories of
the company, especially to those in
Hongkong.

Dispute Explained
Commenting on the dispute over
wage restoration, the statement dis-
closed that shortly after the war
broke out, the Company was com-
pelled to reduce the employees' wages
on a "pyramid" scale—the lower
the pay check, the less the reduction
and the higher the pay check the
greater the reduction.
Workers whose pay was below $20
per month were given no reduction
at all while the burden of the re-
duction was assumed by employees
on the higher wages bracket, the
statement added. This rule was
put into effect in April.

Wages Increased
Early in July, the Company was
able to give a 10 per cent
increase to the reduced wages of
all employees.

（右下角手写批注：7/12 / Life / 8 2/12）

工人罢工

商务印书馆工厂
停工两小时

要求恢复
旧有工资

相信纠纷
解决遥遥无期

（右上角印章内容：S. D. REGISTRY / No. S. B. D. - 06644 / Date ____）

商务印书馆工厂的六百名工人于昨日清晨举行了两小时的静坐罢工，此前他们与公司就恢复工人工资等级至战前水平进行的谈判未能成功。

工人与公司之间的纠纷始于两周前，当时工人代表向公司提出了以下要求：
1. 承认“商务印书馆工人合作协会”，即工人新组建的工会；
2. 提供补贴以覆盖该协会的开支；以及
3. 将工人工资恢复至战前水平。

公司立场强硬
在收到这三项要求后，公司官员与目前身处香港的该公司总裁王云五先生取得了联系。据《字林西报》获悉，王先生回复指示官员称，“鉴于公司目前已面临的困难，接受工人的条件无异于自杀。”
根据总裁的指示，并以该工会在法律上不存在为由，公司在沪官员拒绝与工人代表进行谈判。

发表声明
在公司昨晚发表的一份官方声明中，阐述了其关于当前与工人纠纷的立场。
在解释为何不将工人工资恢复至战前水平时，该声明回顾了公司因中日敌对行动而遭受的损失金额。
据悉，由于公司在闸北的工厂遭到轰炸以及梧州分馆被毁，公司遭受了高达 **〔此处转录不清〕** 的损失。
声明接着称，公司遭受的损失并非实际损失，而是账面损失，据称这些损失落在了股东的肩上。

遭受重大损失
声明补充说，由于公司损失惨重，公司被迫将资本从5,000,000美元减至2,500,000美元。减资是通过注销50%的攀升外汇来实现的。
声明还补充说，该公司在中国各地的30家分馆中，目前仍在运营的不足十家，甚至它们的销售收入也远低于战前水平。

工人待遇良好
关于公司对工人的待遇，声明透露，尽管生产成本上升且销售回报减少，公司实际上并未解雇任何员工。
声明称，当上海爆发战事时，公司的工厂被迫停止运营。然而，工人并未被完全解雇，而是获得了一定数额的津贴以度过危机。
声明称，所有这些工人现在都已重新受聘，要么在当地工厂复工，要么被派往公司的其他工厂，特别是那些位于香港的工厂。

纠纷说明
在评论关于恢复工资的纠纷时，声明披露，战争爆发后不久，公司被迫按“金字塔”比例降低员工工资——薪水越低，减幅越小；薪水越高，减幅越大。
声明补充说，月薪低于20美元的工人完全没有减薪，而减薪的负担则由高薪阶层的员工承担。这一规定于四月生效。

工资增加
七月初，公司得以将所有员工降低后的工资上调10%。

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

EX-WORKERS OF THE COMMERCIAL PRESS.

Upon enquiries made by our reporter yesterday at the Commercial Press, Ltd., an important official of the concern made the following statement :-
"After the printing plant of the Commercial Press was destroyed during the January 28 Incident, the company was obliged to discharge all its employees. With the approval of the Shanghai City Government, it was laid down that when the company resumed business, 80% of the employees would be reinstated. Actually over 90% of our employees are old employees. The allegations that the company had concluded an agreement with the workers to the effect that the entire body of unemployed hands would be reinstated as soon as the company had recovered 80% of its capital are unfounded. As regards the payment of pensions, the company paid off all the pensions on the instructions of the Social Bureau at the time when the employees were discharged. We have in hand receipts showing that the discharged employees had received their money."

April 18, 1936.

Local Incense Makers - Strike

About 200 out of 500 workers in the employ of local
incense factories declared a strike on April 17 to mark
their opposition to a 20% reduction in their wages.
Of this number, it is reported that about 40 are employed
by factories in the Settlement. These workers continue
on strike this morning, while the remainder are working
as usual.

At 3 p.m. April 17, about 100 of the strikers held
a meeting in the Incense Makers' Union, Zao Kia Road,
Nantao, and passed the following resolutions :-

1. That employers be requested to observe the labour
agreement and to restore the original rate of pay.
2. That wages be granted for the period of strike.
3. That requests for mediation be made to the Chinese
Authorities.
4. That a committee be formed to maintain order for
the period of strike.
5. That a propaganda group and a picketing corps, each
consisting of twenty members, be organized.

Commercial Press Ltd. - Ex-workers demand reinstatement

Six delegates of the ex-workers of the Commercial
Press called on the management of the Company at the Sales
Office, 211 Honan Road, at 4 p.m. April 17 with the object
of obtaining an answer to their demand for reinstatement.
They were received by two representatives of the
Management who, however, only promised to give preference
to the ex-workers when there were vacancies in the Company.
The delegates withdrew at 5.30 p.m.
At 10 p.m. April 17 some sixty ex-workers assembled
in the Sales Office and demanded a satisfactory answer to
their demand. Despite the advice of their delegates
urging them to return home and wait for further information,
the ex-workers were still on the premises at 10.40 p.m.

April 16, 1936. Afternoon Translation. （印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... REGISTRY. No. ... 4395 ...）

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:

THE EX-WORKERS OF THE COMMERCIAL PRESS

The Commercial Press Ltd. is the biggest printing concern in China.
During the January 28 Incident, the printing plant of the Commercial Press was totally destroyed by gun fire. Subsequently the company resumed business, but the services of a number of the employees were dispensed with. An agreement was drawn up between the employers and these employees to the effect that the latter would be reinstated as soon as the business of the company improves to the condition that it was in prior to the outbreak of the January 28 Incident. The business of the company has since recovered, yet several hundred of these workers have not yet been given work. Some time ago they detailed representatives to make an appeal to the company for assistance. The appeal was referred to the Board of Directors but the latter failed to give a satisfactory reply.

Shortly after 1 p.m. yesterday about 400 of the workers who have not been reinstated by the company gathered at places along Honan Road and Chiaotung Road near the Sales Office of the Commercial Press. Upon learning of this, Chinese and foreign police of the International Settlement arrived to maintain peace and order.

Yuan Shih Shing (袁士興), Hsu Chi Tseng (徐積曾) and two other representatives of the male workers and Tsu Ah Voong (朱阿鳳) and Moo Yueh Oou (穆月娥), the representatives of the female workers, called on the management of the company and were received by Koo Ping Yuan (顧秉元) and Hsu Pah Tsa (許伯慈) as the General Manager was out on business. The callers submitted the following two demands :-
(1) That the savings and pensions of the workers be issued.
(2) That the unemployed workers be reinstated.
The two officials promised to refer the demands to the General Manager after which a written reply would be given.

The representatives then summoned all the workers to Chiaotung Road and informed them of the result of the interview.

After waiting a considerable time for the return of the General Manager, the workers finally requested the management to give careful consideration to their demands for three days and that they would call again at 10 a.m. April 18 and wait on Chiaotung Road for a reply.

Representatives of the workers made the following statement:- "When the company resumed business, an agreement was reached between the employers and the labourers at the Municipal City Government to the effect that all unemployed hands are to be taken on for work as soon as the company has recovered 50% of its capital. Originally, the capital of the company was $5,000,000 but it has now recovered $3,000,000 of the capital. Furthermore, the number of new hands and apprentices employed by the company is greater than the number of old hands. The company has not yet announced any plans regarding the repayment of the savings and pensions of the unemployed."

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

商务印书馆前雇员

商务印书馆有限公司是中国最大的印刷企业。
在一·二八事变期间，商务印书馆的印刷厂被炮火彻底摧毁。随后公司恢复了营业，但解雇了一批员工。雇主与这些员工之间达成了一项协议，规定一旦公司业务恢复到一·二八事变爆发前的状况，就将复职这些员工。此后公司业务已恢复，但仍有数百名工人未获工作安排。前段时间，他们派出代表向公司求助。该请求被转交董事会，但后者未能给予令人满意的答复。

昨天下午1点过后不久，约400名未被公司复职的工人聚集在商务印书馆销售办事处附近的河南路和交通路沿线各处。得知此事后，公共租界的中外警察赶到现场维持治安秩序。

男工代表袁士兴（Yuan Shih Shing）、徐积曾（Hsu Chi Tseng）及另外两人，以及女工代表朱阿凤（Tsu Ah Voong）和穆月娥（Moo Yueh Oou），前往拜访公司管理层，并由顾秉元（Koo Ping Yuan）和许伯慈（Hsu Pah Tsa）接待，因为总经理外出公干。来访者提出了以下两项要求：
(1) 发放工人的储蓄金和养老金。
(2) 复职失业工人。
两位官员承诺将要求转呈总经理，随后将给予书面答复。

代表们随后将所有工人召集到交通路，并向他们通报了面谈结果。

在等待总经理返回相当长一段时间后，工人们最终要求管理层在三天内仔细考虑他们的要求，并表示他们将于4月18日上午10时再次前来，在交通路等候答复。

工人代表发表了如下声明：“公司恢复营业时，雇主与劳工在市市政府达成协议，规定一旦公司收回50%的资本，所有失业工人将被录用工作。公司原资本为5,000,000美元，现已收回3,000,000美元资本。此外，公司雇佣的新手和学徒人数多于老员工人数。公司尚未公布任何关于偿还未就业工人储蓄金和养老金的计划。”

China Times (Editorial) :-

IS JAPAN FOR OR AGAINST THE REDS?

Japanese newspapers are exerting every effort to provoke ill-feeling between China and Japan. The Japanese authorities are entangling China over the question of united Sino-Japanese defence against the Communists.

As regards the invasion of Shansi by the Red bandits, the Japanese declare that the penetration of Red influence into China would endanger the safety of North China. Not satisfied with intentionally spreading this smoke screen, the Japanese authorities eventually fabricated reports relating to a Sino-Russian Secret Agreement and later spread reports that Chinese military leaders would accept Communism.

The Government troops are making advance in the bandit suppression campaign thereby proving that the reports spread by Japanese are untrue.

The Shanghai "Mainichi" recently published reports to the effect that Chinese military leaders had concluded a secret agreement with the Communist armies, that the Nanking troops had entered Shansi because of the victory of the Communist armies and that the advance to the North of the Nanking troops is intended as a threat against General Sung Cheh Yuan, General Han Fu Chu and others in North China. There is a political significance behind this malicious propaganda.

If Japan really desires to ensure the safety of East Asia, she should respect the integrity of China's territory and sovereign rights, cease fabricating rumours and restore Sino-Japanese relations to what they were before the September 18 Incident.

When the Government troops were about to wipe out the bandits in Shansi, Japan again fabricated rumours with the intention of disturbing the relations between the Government and the district authorities. Japan seems to have concluded a secret pact with the bandits.

We strongly believe that the Chinese people and the authorities in North China fully realise this and will not be misled by rumours.

《字林西报》（社论）：-

日本是支持还是反对赤色分子？

日本报纸正竭尽全力挑拨中日之间的恶感。日本当局就中日联合防共问题与中国纠缠不清。

关于赤匪入侵山西一事，日本人宣称，赤色势力渗入中国将危及华北的安全。日本当局不满足于故意散布这种烟幕弹，随后又捏造了有关《中俄秘密协定》的报道，继而散布中国军事领袖将接受共产主义的消息。

政府军队在剿匪战役中取得进展，从而证明日本散布的报道不实。

上海《每日新闻》最近刊登报道，称中国军事领袖已与共产党军队达成秘密协定，南京部队进入山西是因为共产党军队的胜利，而南京部队向北推进意在威胁华北的宋哲元将军、韩复榘将军等人。这种恶意宣传背后有着政治意义。

如果日本真的希望确保东亚的安全，她就应该尊重中国的领土完整和主权，停止制造谣言，并将中日关系恢复到九一八事变之前的状态。

当政府军队即将肃清山西的匪徒时，日本再次制造谣言，意图扰乱政府与地方当局之间的关系。日本似乎已与匪徒达成了秘密 pact。

我们坚信，中国人民和华北当局充分认识到这一点，不会被谣言所误导。

April 2, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Lih Pao (立报):

CLASH BETWEEN WORKERS & POLICE

Prior to the January 28 Incident, the main factory of the Commercial Press, Ltd. on Paoshan Road employed about 800 workers. As the main factory was destroyed during the Incident, most of these 800 workers have been out of employment.

Shortly after 10 a.m. yesterday a number of workers went to the Sales Office of the Commercial Press, Ltd. on Honan Road and demanded that they be given first chance of selection for employment. As the doors to the premises were crowded with workers and as this might affect the business of the store, the management sent a telephone message to the Police asking for assistance.

Upon receipt of this telephone message, the Police despatched three police vans and several tens of detectives and policemen to quell the crowd. As the large crowd was obstructing the traffic, the Police dispersed it by means of force. A minor clash occurred between the workers and the Police. A representative of the workers named Kao Sih Tao (高濤), ex-worker of the Printing Department of the Commercial Press Works, was struck with a baton and injured in the left arm. Several old female workers were also injured when they were pushed and trodden upon by the crowd. Kao Sih Tao was later sent to St. Luke's Hospital for treatment.

In an interview with Hsu Chi Tseng (徐季崢), a representative of the discharged workers, Wong Yuin Woo (王雲五), General Manager of the Commercial Press, Ltd., stated that as the matter is one of some importance, a reply would be given the men on April 6 after the matter had been brought up for discussion at a meeting of the Board of Directors on April 4.

JAPAN'S ACTIVITIES IN SOUTH FOKIEN

The autonomy movement in Fukien Province is nearing completion. Fukien has been a centre of activities of a certain nation since the September 18th Incident. For this reason, Fukien Province is already being regarded as a protectorate of that nation. The situation in the south of Fukien is most serious.

Amoy and Changmeng are the two principal harbours of Fukien Province. Formerly the Chinese Authorities in Amoy and the Customs used to be notified beforehand by the Consul of a foreign nation when its warships desire to enter any one of the harbours, but since 1934, this practice has not been observed. The warships of a certain nation now have free access to these harbours and no notice is sent to the Chinese district authorities.

《立报》：

工人与警察发生冲突

在一·二八事变之前，位于宝山路上的商务印书馆有限公司总厂雇佣了约800名工人。由于总厂在事变中被毁，这800名工人中的大多数一直失业。

昨天上午10点后不久，一些工人前往位于河南路的商务印书馆有限公司销售部，要求给予他们优先录用的机会。由于大门处挤满了工人，且这可能影响商店的业务，管理层打电话给警察局请求协助。

接到电话后，警察局派遣了三辆警车和数十名侦探及警察来驱散人群。由于大量人群阻碍交通，警察使用武力驱散了人群。工人与警察之间发生了轻微冲突。一名名叫高濤（Kao Sih Tao）的工人代表，系商务印书馆印刷部的前工人，被警棍击中，左臂受伤。几名老年女工在被人群推挤和踩踏时也受了伤。高濤随后被送往圣路加医院接受治疗。

在接受被解雇工人代表徐季崢（Hsu Chi Tseng）采访时，商务印书馆有限公司总经理王雲五（Wong Yuin Woo）表示，由于此事较为重要，将在4月4日董事会会议讨论后，于4月6日向工人们给予答复。

日本在闽南的活动

福建省的自治运动已接近尾声。自九一八事变以来，福建一直是某国活动的中心。因此，福建省已被视为该国的保护国。闽南局势最为严峻。

厦门和漳蒙（Changmeng，音译）是福建省的两个主要港口。以前，当某外国领事馆的军舰希望进入任何一个港口时，通常会事先通知厦门的中国当局和海关，但自1934年以来，这一惯例已不再遵守。某国的军舰现在可以自由进入这些港口，且不向中国地方当局发送任何通知。

Commercial Press - Manager receives threatening letters

Since August 1931 the manager of the Commercial
Press, 211 Honan Road, has been in receipt of several
threatening letters purporting to emanate from the
workers of the factory who were paid off following
the destruction of the premises on Pachan Road during
